rows.description: I see my parent growing frail and feel afraid of losing them and of my own inadequacy. I spend real time now, ask about their wishes, and accept that I cannot stop ageing; avoiding visits out of fear only builds regret.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, gratitude, guilt, pride, resentment
related mind states: fear, insecurity, regret

rows.description: My parent leans on me for money, medical trips, or company and I feel both love and being trapped. I share the load with siblings, set realistic limits, and remember that saying I need help is not disloyalty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, fear, gratitude, guilt, pride, resentment

rows.description: My ageing parent refuses help, skips medicines, or resents advice and I feel frustrated and worried. I respect their dignity, offer choices, not orders, and involve their doctor or a trusted relative rather than fighting every day.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, gratitude, guilt, resentment
related mind states: admiration, anger, anxiety, pride

rows.description: I live far from my parents for work and feel guilty for not being there. I stay in regular contact, arrange practical support, and make honest visits; guilt is useful when it moves action and harmful when it just torments.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, gratitude, pride, resentment

rows.description: I do most of the caregiving while my sibling does little and I feel used and bitter. I ask them clearly for specific tasks or money, not a vague sense of duty, and accept help from outside if they stay absent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, gratitude, guilt, pride

rows.description: As my parent needs me, I remember how much they gave and feel deep gratitude. Repaying is not bookkeeping; I care with patience and warmth, and I also look after my own health so I can keep going.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, guilt, pride, resentment

rows.description: My parent expects me to give up my job, city, or marriage plans to look after them and calls it my duty. I feel love and pressure both. I look for arrangements that honour both their needs and my life and speak honestly about limits.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, gratitude, guilt, pride

rows.description: I watch a parent lose strength or memory and feel helpless and sometimes irritated, then ashamed of the irritation. Both are normal. I get information, share the load, and treat them with patience and dignity.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, fear, gratitude, guilt, pride

rows.description: I feel I was always compared with my brother or sister and now we compete over family property or attention. I remember the bond behind the contest; the wise move is to speak fairly and openly, not to keep score for decades.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, favouritism, grief, guilt, protectiveness, resentment

rows.description: My sibling resents me for being favoured, or for having more, and I feel guilty and puzzled. I listen without defending, acknowledge what was unfair, and do not buy peace by giving up what I honestly need.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, favouritism, grief, guilt, protectiveness, rivalry
related mind states: guilt, confusion, calm, resentment
